senses.gloss: dṛś, cf. peṭaṃ (Sanskrit udaraṃ) darśayitum (EI 11), literally, ‘to show one's belley’; but actually ‘to ask for the means of livelihood’.

dṛṣṭa (EI 3, 23; CII 3; etc.), Prakrit diṭṭham, ‘has been seen’, i. e. ‘found correct and approved’, found on some copper-plate grants indicating the approval of the proper authorities endorsed on the original document later engraved on the plates. Cf. ni (an abbreviation of nibaddha or nirīkṣiṭa) in certain medieval copper-plate grants of Eastern India. In dṛṣṭa-pañcāśat-padāti (LP), dṛṣṭa-ghoṭaka (LP), etc., the word dṛṣṭa indicates that money should be paid after actually seeing the foot-soldiers and horses in question.

dṛṣṭi (IE 7-1-2), ‘two’; cf. netra; also darśana, ‘six’.
 (IA 19), Buddhist; theory or doctrine; a peculiar or heretical doctrine.
